title: A ciphered reader's judgment in the Wolfenbüttel alchemical miscellany

steps.what: Distinguished numeral-like shapes in the four lines and two following cipher words. Several marked signs were initially conflated.
Searched keys against word-internal and boundary four-letter frequencies. The German trial recovered also, dises, ist and distil.
Resolved the shared letters of mich, der rechte and philosophei against the enlarged folio. The first group in line three remains uncertain.
The resulting key reads Latin words including sulphurem and salem on f. 105r and the body/soul labels on f. 104v.
Surveyed the complete HAB facsimile and located earlier marginal annotations in the same cipher.

The dotted circle gives w in weisse on scan 00030 and in worden and wol on 00155. The rare consonant signs in the coin name on 00155 recur in wec?? on 00218. Historical weckg supports reading the noun as Weg, while the order of the two proposed consonant values remains provisional.
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 48 tokens, 16 types, de-1500s order 4: reading -1.993 per letter; Verdict: too short.

Recounted by the README word rule (sure words only): 8 of 11 cipher words read with nothing supplied; da[s], wec[gk] and philo[s]ophei are holes. Three holes exceed the short-text floor of two, so the class changed from read to read in part. No values changed.

Scope decision after the claims review: this record and the page cover the four-line note on f. 103v only. Catalogue 3897 is kept and narrowed to the cipher groups of the separate Latin recipe on f. 105r, which read only in fragments (outcome 'attempted, open'), instead of being removed. Open items of this record stay the four signs J, j, F and E (too short).

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.993; polyphony 0.0; 4 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached n/a

outcome.notes: Read in part by the README word rule (sure words only, 19 Nov 2026): 8 of the 11 cipher words of the four-line judgment on f. 103v come out of the key with nothing supplied (0.727). Three words carry letters supplied in the reading: da[s], wec[gk] and philo[s]ophei. The short-text floor allows at most two holes in a text under 40 words, so it does not apply. The record covers the four-line document. Other cipher annotations supplied comparisons. The cipher groups of the separate recipe on f. 105r stay open as catalogue 3897.
outcome.method_basis: The first German words emerged from a substitution search on the transcribed cipher. Other inscriptions in the same volume checked and extended the mapping.

texts.label: The four-line note on folio 103v
texts.summary: A reader judges the preceding alchemical work to be the true way of philosophy. Eight of the eleven words come out of the key; three carry supplied letters, so the note is read in part.

reading_review.note: One continuous German sentence. The strict key leaves four signs open and the reading marks all four.

outcome.fraction_read_source: 48 of 52 signs take a value from key.tsv (validation.tsv; the two descended 7-like signs and the last two signs of wec?? are open). By words, 8 of 11 cipher words are read with nothing supplied (0.727), which decides the class.

gaps.item: the two descended 7-like signs J and j (s in da[s] and philo[s]ophei)
gaps.detail: each occurs once in the four lines and no annotation read elsewhere in the volume gives either shape a value; s is supplied from the sense

gaps.item: the last two signs of wec?? (F and E, read g and k)
gaps.detail: their values rest on one coin name on image 00155 (pfenni?c?), where they stand on either side of c, while the 1432 spelling weckg has the opposite order; no other occurrence fixes them
